subject.title: Telegram should default to allowlist mode with owner ID

question: Should Telegram first-run setup replace default pairing with token-verified owner capture and allowlist config, or keep pairing as the default trust model?
rationale: The requested behavior improves safe defaults but changes first-run authorization, setup UX, and config/default behavior, which repository policy treats as compatibility-sensitive and security/product-reviewed.

options.title: Token-Verified Allowlist Onboarding
options.body: Generate a short setup token, capture only the Telegram sender who sends it, and write `dmPolicy="allowlist"` plus numeric `allowFrom` for fresh setups while preserving explicit pairing configs.

options.title: Keep Pairing Default
options.body: Keep pairing as the default and rely on warnings, docs, and manual allowlist setup for private bots.

options.title: Fold Into Bootstrap Work
options.body: Let the broader one-line bootstrap issue own the user-facing flow while this issue remains the Telegram-specific requirements reference.

recommendation.title: Token-Verified Allowlist Onboarding
recommendation.body: Generate a short setup token, capture only the Telegram sender who sends it, and write `dmPolicy="allowlist"` plus numeric `allowFrom` for fresh setups while preserving explicit pairing configs.
